artiest/nick-en-simon.text:
Nick & Simon was a Dutch singing and presenting duo from Volendam, consisting of Nick Schilder and Simon Keizer. Both come from well-known Volendam musical families. Nick made his first television appearance on Idols, the Dutch version of Idol, where he finished eleventh. Shortly afterwards he and Simon began performing together. In 2006 they became popular in the Netherlands, and in 2007 they were the most booked act in the country.

Their first album, Nick & Simon, was released in 2006, followed by Vandaag in 2007. The album Luister, from 2009, went double platinum within four months. Fier followed in 2010, Sterker in 2012, Open in 2015 and Aangenaam in 2017, alongside Christmas albums and the German-language Ein Neuer Tag in 2014. Their hits included Kijk omhoog and Pak maar m'n hand. In June 2011 they went in search of the American Dream in a television documentary. They were coaches in the first three seasons of The Voice of Holland and presented various television programmes and music documentaries.

The group made Dutch-language pop music for a broad audience, with melodic songs and a pronounced attachment to their home town. In the end the duo decided to split after the Nu of Ooit tour, because both men wanted more room for a career of their own. Their success shows how strongly Dutch-language pop grew in the years after 2005.
artiest/nick-en-simon.listen: Listen to Kijk omhoog and notice the melody and the singing: how do the two voices share the lines, and what makes the chorus so easy to sing along to?

artiest/nick-larocca.text: Cornettist Nick LaRocca was the leader of the Original Dixieland Jass Band, a group of five white musicians from New Orleans. In February 1917 the band recorded Livery Stable Blues and Dixie Jass Band One-Step for Victor in New York: the first jazz record. The record sold very well and made the word jazz known overnight. In 1919 the band also performed in London. Their playing was mainly loud and comical, with animal noises imitated on the instruments. LaRocca later claimed that white musicians had invented jazz, which is not true: Black musicians in New Orleans had been playing that way for years before. The group is important above all as the beginning of jazz on record.
artiest/nick-larocca.listen: Listen to the animal noises in Livery Stable Blues: this was entertainment, too.

artiest/nick-lowe.text:
Nick Lowe, born on 24 March 1949, is an English singer, musician and producer. He plays guitar, bass guitar, piano and harmonica and is regarded as a well-known figure in pub rock, power pop and new wave. His career began in 1967 in Kippington Lodge, together with his school friend Brinsley Schwarz. At the end of 1969 the band was renamed Brinsley Schwarz and played country and blues rock. In 1975 Lowe left and became bassist and singer of Rockpile, alongside Dave Edmunds.

In August 1976 So It Goes was released, the first single on Stiff Records, where Lowe was also house producer. Among other things he produced the first album by The Damned and work by Elvis Costello and Graham Parker. His first solo albums were Jesus of Cool and Pure Pop for Now People, both from 1978, followed by Labour of Lust in 1979. That album includes Cruel to Be Kind, his best-known song, alongside I Love the Sound of Breaking Glass. He also wrote (What's So Funny 'Bout) Peace, Love, and Understanding, which became a hit for Costello, and I Knew the Bride (When She Used to Rock 'n' Roll), a hit for Dave Edmunds. There is only one official Rockpile album, Seconds of Pleasure from 1980, because the two singers were under contract to different record companies.

In 1979 Lowe married the country singer Carlene Carter, and later played and recorded with Johnny Cash. His strength lay in short, melodic songs with a dry humour, and in his role as a producer and maker of records that paved the way for new wave.
artiest/nick-lowe.listen: Listen to Cruel to Be Kind and notice the tight, cheerful pop structure: short verses, a chorus that sticks in your head and a clear band underneath. Hear how little frill the song needs.

artiest/nick-phoenix.text:
Nick Phoenix, born on 25 August 1967 in London, is a British composer and pianist and co-founder of the production music company Two Steps from Hell. Since 1997 he has been making music for film trailers and producing virtual instrument libraries for EastWest Sounds. In total he has more than twelve hundred scores and placements to his name, most of them for trailers.

In 2006 he founded Two Steps from Hell together with his business partner Thomas Bergersen. In 2010 the two released the album Invincible, after which further releases followed, including Archangel and SkyWorld. Both albums reached the iTunes top 100 in the Soundtracks category. In 2013 Phoenix performed with Bergersen in a live concert at the Walt Disney Concert Hall. The same year saw the release of his solo album Speed of Sound, a hybrid of electronic music and orchestra. With his band Crater Mountain he released the classic rock album Hillbilly Starship in 2014. He also wrote a book, Colin Frake on Fire Mountain, with an accompanying soundtrack, and a sequel in 2017, Colin Frake Asclepius.

Phoenix is important for the way film music sounds today: big, orchestral and built for a short, spectacular edit. His work shows how trailer music has become a branch of pop and film music in its own right, with listeners who seek out the music apart from the film.
artiest/nick-phoenix.listen: Listen to a piece from Speed of Sound and notice how electronic sounds and orchestral instruments weave together. Ask yourself what images the music evokes, even without a film.

artiest/nicky-hopkins.text:
Nicky Hopkins was an English pianist and organist, born in 1944 in Perivale, near London. He had been playing the piano since the age of three and won a scholarship to the Royal Academy of Music. For much of his life he suffered from Crohn's disease. Because of the complications and the many operations, touring was difficult, and so he worked mainly as a session musician in the studio.

In the mid-1960s he was one of the most sought-after session pianists in London. From 1967 he played with The Rolling Stones, with striking parts in She's a Rainbow, from Their Satanic Majesties Request, and in Sympathy for the Devil. He appears on most Stones albums between 1967 and 1981, and his playing on Exile on Main St. in particular is often mentioned. He also played on records by The Kinks and The Who, and the electric piano solo in the Beatles' Revolution is his. In 1968 he became a member of the Jeff Beck Group, and then of Quicksilver Messenger Service. He performed at Woodstock with Jefferson Airplane.

Hopkins adapted to every kind of song: ballads, hard rock and acoustic work. Ray Davies of The Kinks said that he only played when it was needed, but that his contribution then really made a difference. He is regarded as one of the best studio pianists in the history of rock. Under his own name he made, among others, The Revolutionary Piano of Nicky Hopkins (1966) and The Tin Man Was a Dreamer (1973). Later he wrote film music, with particular success in Japan. He died in 1994 in Nashville, aged fifty.
artiest/nicky-hopkins.listen: In She's a Rainbow, listen to Hopkins's bright, skipping piano figure, which opens the song and keeps returning. Notice how the piano blends with the strings and the Mellotron, and yet remains the most recognisable part.

artiest/nico.text:
Nico, born Christa Päffgen, was a German singer, songwriter, actress and model. She was born in Cologne in 1938 and grew up during and after the Second World War, partly in Berlin. As a teenager she became a fashion model. Later she worked in Paris and New York, where she took acting lessons and appeared in films such as Federico Fellini's La Dolce Vita (1960) and Andy Warhol's Chelsea Girls (1966).

Through Warhol, who managed the group, she became the singer of The Velvet Underground. On the debut The Velvet Underground & Nico (1967), with Warhol's banana on the sleeve, she sings three songs: Femme Fatale, All Tomorrow's Parties and I'll Be Your Mirror. One critic described her voice as half goddess, half icicle. That same year she made the solo album Chelsea Girl, with songs by Bob Dylan and Tim Hardin, among others, but she was unhappy with the orchestral arrangements.

Encouraged by Jim Morrison, she began writing her own songs, built around the harmonium, a small pump organ that became her trademark. The Marble Index (1968), arranged by John Cale, sounds dark and is influenced by classical music. Desertshore (1970) and The End... (1974) followed. With her dark clothes and severe appearance she anticipated gothic rock. Artists such as Siouxsie and the Banshees, The Cure, Morrissey and Björk were influenced by her. In 1988 she fell off her bicycle on Ibiza; she died of a brain haemorrhage, aged 49.
artiest/nico.listen: In All Tomorrow's Parties, listen to Nico's voice: heavy, flat and almost without vibrato, with a German accent. Notice the piano that keeps repeating the same hard chords, which gives the song something compelling.

artiest/nicola-piovani.text: Nicola Piovani was born in Rome in 1946. In 1967 he took his piano diploma at the conservatory in Milan and studied orchestration with the Greek composer Manos Hadjidakis. Since 1968 he has written music for more than 190 films, as well as for theatre, opera and the concert hall. He worked with the Taviani brothers, among other things on Kaos (1984). For the last three films of Federico Fellini, Ginger e Fred, Intervista and La voce della luna, he took the place of Nino Rota. For Nanni Moretti he wrote, among others, La stanza del figlio (2001). For Roberto Benigni's La vita è bella (1997) he received an Oscar for best original score. In 2008 he became a Chevalier of the French Ordre des Arts et des Lettres.
artiest/nicola-piovani.listen: Listen to the simple, songlike melodies in small ensembles, often piano or accordion with a few strings, which hover between wistfulness and humour.

artiest/nicolas-godin.text:
Nicolas Godin, born on 25 December 1969 in Le Chesnay, near Paris, is a French musician best known as one half of the duo Air. He studied architecture in Versailles, where he met the mathematics student Jean-Benoît Dunckel. Before Air they played together in the band Orange. The name Air does not stand for Amour, Imagination, Rêve, but refers to the airy sound of their music.

It began as a solo project. At the request of a childhood friend, Godin wrote a track for a compilation on the small label Source: Modulor Mix, a tribute to Le Corbusier, recorded on a Portastudio. It appeared in 1995 on Source Lab and in 1996 in a new version on Mo' Wax. He then brought in Dunckel, and the duo made maxi-singles for Source. In 1998 the debut album Moon Safari was released, with the singles Sexy Boy, Kelly Watch the Stars and All I Need. With its blend of synthesizers, strings and guitar, it was a remarkable record for the electronic music of its time.

On 18 September 2015 Godin released his first solo album, Contrepoint, inspired by the music of Johann Sebastian Bach. Concrete and Glass followed in 2020, and then the music for the documentary Fire of Love, on which he worked in 2022. Godin shows how French electronic pop can combine classical melodies, architectural thinking and a soft, melodic sound.
artiest/nicolas-godin.listen: Listen to Sexy Boy by Air and notice the layers of synthesizer, strings and guitar that together create a dreamlike atmosphere. Then find a piece from Contrepoint and hear where Bach shines through.

artiest/nicole-croisille.text:
Nicole Croisille was a French singer and actress. She was born on 9 October 1936 in Neuilly-sur-Seine and died on 4 June 2025 in Saint-Cloud, aged 88. Between 1961 and 2005 she appeared in twenty-four films, and from 1961 she recorded several albums. Her best-known work is probably the soundtrack of Un Homme et Une Femme, Claude Lelouch's film from 1966. In it she sang a solo, Today It's You, and sang several songs together with Pierre Barouh.

In 1974 she tried to represent France at the Eurovision Song Contest with Tu m'avais dit and Je t'aime un point c'est tout, but in the end Dani was chosen, who did not take part because of the death of Georges Pompidou. Among her best-known records are I'll Never Leave You, Téléphone-Moi, Une Femme avec Toi, J'ai besoin de Toi, J'ai besoin de Lui and Parlez-moi de Lui, the title of her 1974 album. Her single Woman in Your Arms reached number 71 in Australia in May 1976. Later she made jazz-oriented records, such as Jazzille from 1987, Black & Blanche from 1990 and Nougaro, le jazz et moi from 2006.

Nicole Croisille stands for the French chanson that opens itself to jazz and film music. Her voice was heard worldwide thanks to Lelouch's film, one of the best-known French films of the 1960s. She shows how film music and song art continually influenced each other in France.
artiest/nicole-croisille.listen: Listen to her solo Today It's You from the film Un Homme et Une Femme and notice how she gives colour to a film scene with her voice alone. Hear how the accompanying film music stays soft and floating.

artiest/nightwish.text:
Nightwish is a Finnish symphonic metal band from Kitee. Keyboardist Tuomas Holopainen came up with the project in 1996 at a campfire. He was thinking of acoustic atmospheric music with guitar, flutes, strings, piano and above all a female singer. Together with guitarist Emppu Vuorinen and singer Tarja Turunen, the foundation was laid. Later drummer Jukka Nevalainen and bassist Sami Vänskä joined, and in 2001 Marko Hietala took over the bass and part of the vocals. The debut album Angels Fall First was released in 1997. Oceanborn (1998), Wishmaster (2000), Century Child (2002) and Once (2004) followed, which made the band known outside Finland as well.

Nightwish's sound sets the heavy guitars and drums of metal beside Turunen's classically trained voice and the orchestra. On Century Child a real Finnish orchestra played along for the first time. The band's own version of The Phantom of the Opera became a fan favourite. Nemo, chosen as an example in the course, comes from Once, released in 2004.

In 2005 Turunen left. Anette Olzon took her place and sang on Dark Passion Play (2007) and Imaginaerum (2011). Floor Jansen has been the singer since 2013, and Endless Forms Most Beautiful (2015), Human. :II: Nature. (2020) and Yesterwynde (2024) followed later. Nightwish is one of Finland's best-selling acts and was inducted into the Finnish Music Hall of Fame in 2018. For the history of pop, the band shows how metal and classical music can also find a large audience together.
artiest/nightwish.listen: Listen to Nemo. Notice the contrast between the heavy guitars and the clear, classical-sounding vocals, and how the keyboards give the whole an orchestral sound.

artiest/nikolaj-rimski-korsakov.text:
Nikolai Andreyevich Rimsky-Korsakov was born on 18 March 1844 in Tikhvin, east of Saint Petersburg, into a noble Russian family. He died on 21 June 1908. He belonged to The Five, the group of Russian composers who wanted to develop a national style. For a long time he combined composing and teaching with a career in the military: first as an officer in the Russian navy, later as a civilian inspector of the naval bands. There he learned a great deal about the sound of woodwind and brass. From 1871 he was professor of composition, harmony and orchestration at the Saint Petersburg Conservatory. Through rigorous self-study he mastered Western methods in the space of three years.

His best-known orchestral works are Capriccio Espagnol, the Russian Easter Festival Overture and the symphonic suite Scheherazade, which was recorded many times in the course of the twentieth century. He also wrote fifteen operas. He liked to use fairy tales and folk motifs and added exotic harmonies, melodies and rhythms, an approach known as musical orientalism. His love of the sea may have contributed to Sadko and Scheherazade.

Rimsky-Korsakov prepared works by The Five for performance, which brought them into the standard repertoire, although his edition of Mussorgsky is controversial. As a teacher he trained an entire generation of younger composers. He is regarded as the most important builder of what classical audiences call the Russian style, and his colourful orchestration is often held up as an example, including for later film music.
artiest/nikolaj-rimski-korsakov.listen: Listen to Scheherazade and notice the violin solo, which represents the narrator of the fairy tales, and how the woodwinds and harp lay their own colours around it. Watch how he creates atmosphere with the instruments.

artiest/nikolaus-harnoncourt.text:
Nikolaus Harnoncourt was an Austrian conductor who became known above all for his historically informed performances. He was born in Berlin on 6 December 1929, grew up in Graz and studied cello and viola da gamba at the music academy in Vienna. He died on 5 March 2016. At first he worked as a cellist in the orchestra. In 1953 he founded his own ensemble on period instruments, Concentus Musicus Wien, and with it he became a pioneer of the early music movement.

His speciality was the Baroque, but later he extended his repertoire to Classical and early Romantic music. Around 1970 he began conducting opera and concerts, soon also with large symphony orchestras, in leading concert halls and at festivals. In 2001 and 2003 he conducted the New Year's Concert in Vienna. His recordings include Brandenburgische Konzerte in 1967, Matthäus-Passion in 1971, Le quattro stagioni in 1977 and Messiah in 1983. With Gustav Leonhardt he recorded all 193 of Bach's cantatas. He also wrote several books, mostly on performance practice and musical aesthetics.

Harnoncourt showed that early music, played on period instruments and with a sharp eye for performance, can sound different from the Romantic tradition. That made him important for anyone who wants to know how music from the past may originally have sounded, and it changed the way Baroque music was played.
artiest/nikolaus-harnoncourt.listen: Listen to a Brandenburg Concerto in his 1967 recording and notice the sound of the old instruments and the lively, incisive rhythm. Compare that with a performance on modern instruments.

artiest/nile-rodgers.text:
Nile Rodgers is an American guitarist, songwriter and producer. He was born in New York in 1952 and grew up in Greenwich Village, where jazz musicians such as Thelonious Monk were regular visitors. He played flute and clarinet at first and took up the guitar at sixteen. As a teenager he played in African, Latin, jazz and boogaloo bands. In 1970 he met the bassist Bernard Edwards. Together they started the Big Apple Band, which in 1977 became Chic.

Chic blended jazz, soul and funk with elegant melodies. After the 1977 debut came Le Freak and I Want Your Love on C'est Chic (1978), and Good Times on Risqué (1979). The groove of Good Times was used in the Sugarhill Gang's Rapper's Delight and is one of the most sampled songs ever. The sound revolved around two things: Rodgers's short, rhythmic guitar playing, known as chucking, and Edwards's bouncing bass lines. Together they also wrote and produced for others, such as We Are Family by Sister Sledge and Upside Down and I'm Coming Out by Diana Ross.

After the end of Chic in 1983, Rodgers became a much-in-demand producer. He produced David Bowie's Let's Dance, Madonna's Like a Virgin and work by Duran Duran and INXS. Later he played on Daft Punk's Random Access Memories and worked with Beyoncé. His guitar playing links the disco of the 1970s with the dance music of today, and few musicians have helped shape so many hits.
artiest/nile-rodgers.listen: Listen to Le Freak by Chic. Notice Rodgers's short, clipped guitar chords and how Bernard Edwards's bass keeps bouncing around them.

artiest/nils-aslak-valkeapaa.text:
Nils-Aslak Valkeapää, in Northern Sami Áilu and under the artist name Áillohaš, was a Finnish-Sami writer, musician and visual artist. He was born in 1943 in Enontekiö, into a family of nomadic Sami reindeer herders, and died on 26 November 2001. His mother tongue was Northern Sami, but like many Sami children in the 1950s he received no schooling in it, and only as an adult did he learn to write in his own language. He became one of the best-known representatives of Sami culture.

As a musician he first performed as an interpreter of the traditional joik and played a central role in the revival of that genre. His debut record Joikuja appeared in 1968. In 1973, on a retreat with folk and jazz musicians, he was inspired by Dvořák's Symphony No. 9 and the spirituals in it, and so he developed fusion joik. Together with Seppo Paakkunainen he made Juoigansinfonija, a jazz joik symphony. In 1978 came Sámiid eatnan duoddariid. His music was controversial, partly because of the jazz elements and partly because strictly devout Sami often regarded the joik as sinful. From 1968 to 1994 he released thirteen records. Goase Dušše (The Bird Symphony), built from nature sounds from Sápmi, received a special jury prize at the Prix Italia in 1993. In 1994 he performed at the opening of the Winter Olympics in Lillehammer.

For his poetry collection Beaivi, áhčážan he received the Nordic Council Literature Prize in 1991. Mike Oldfield used a recording of Valkeapää in Prayer for the Earth on The Songs of Distant Earth in 1994. Valkeapää brought the joik to a worldwide audience and showed that this ancient form of song can go together with jazz.
artiest/nils-aslak-valkeapaa.listen: Listen to Goase Dušše (The Bird Symphony) and notice how nature sounds form the basis of the piece. Ask yourself where music begins and nature ends.

artiest/nils-petter-molv-r.text:
Nils Petter Molvær, also known as NPM, was born on 18 September 1960 and grew up on the island of Sula in Møre og Romsdal in Norway. He is a jazz trumpeter, composer and producer. At nineteen he left for Trondheim to study jazz at the conservatory. He then played in the groups Jazzpunkensemblet with Jon Eberson and Masqualero, together with Arild Andersen, Jon Christensen and Tore Brunborg. Masqualero, named after a composition by Wayne Shorter that Miles Davis recorded, made several albums for ECM Records.

His debut album Khmer, in 1997, became his most commercially successful record. It blends jazz, rock, electronic soundscapes and hip hop rhythms and sounds very different from the delicate chamber jazz with which ECM was usually associated. Solid Ether followed in 2000, NP3 in 2002, Hamada in 2009 and Switch in 2014, among others. He often works with the guitarist Eivind Aarset and also played with Tabla Beat Science, the group of Zakir Hussain and Bill Laswell. He received the Kongsberg Jazz Award in 1996, the Spellemannprisen in 1997 and the Gammleng-prisen in the jazz category in 1998.

Molvær is regarded as a pioneer of future jazz, a genre that brings jazz and electronics together. His muted trumpet takes on a new role in that music, between beats and digital space. In doing so he showed that jazz can connect with the electronic music of the 1990s.
artiest/nils-petter-molv-r.listen: Listen to a track from Khmer and notice the trumpet set against the electronic sounds and the beats. Ask yourself what you hear as jazz and what as electronics.

artiest/nina-hagen.text:
Nina Hagen, born Catharina Hagen, is a German singer and actress from East Berlin, born in 1955. Her mother was the actress and singer Eva-Maria Hagen, her stepfather the dissident singer Wolf Biermann. In the GDR she became known with the band Automobil. Her song Du hast den Farbfilm vergessen (1974) playfully poked fun at the grey, controlled atmosphere in the country.

In 1976 Biermann was stripped of his East German citizenship, and Hagen followed him to the West. She signed with CBS and came into contact with punk in London. In West Berlin she started the Nina Hagen Band, whose 1978 debut album, with the single TV-Glotzer, sold well and received glowing reviews. What set her apart was her theatrical singing: thanks to her operatic training she could switch within a single song between raw punk vocals and high, operatic flights. In 1979 she left the band.

As a solo artist she made the English-language NunSexMonkRock in 1982, her first album in the American charts, followed by Fearless (1983) and Nina Hagen in Ekstasy (1985). With her statements about spirituality and animal rights and her provocations, she was constantly in the news. She is often called the Godmother of German Punk. Later she voiced characters in the German versions of films such as The Nightmare Before Christmas and made, among other things, Volksbeat (2011) and the gospel album Highway to Heaven (2026). In 2021 Angela Merkel chose Du hast den Farbfilm vergessen for her farewell ceremony.
artiest/nina-hagen.listen: In Du hast den Farbfilm vergessen, hear how Hagen reproaches her boyfriend for forgetting the colour film, so that the holiday photos are only black and white. Notice the cheerful accompaniment and the exaggerated, theatrical singing, in which the mockery of the grey GDR can be heard.

artiest/nina-simone.text: Eunice Waymon from Tryon, North Carolina, wanted to become a concert pianist. When she was rejected by the Curtis Institute in Philadelphia, which she herself attributed to racism, she began playing and singing in bars as Nina Simone. Her first album Little Girl Blue (1958) contained My Baby Just Cares for Me and I Loves You, Porgy, which became a hit. She blended jazz, blues, gospel and classical piano technique. After the church bombing in Birmingham in 1963 she wrote Mississippi Goddam and became a voice of the civil rights movement. Four Women is about four Black women. Later she lived in Africa, Europe and, briefly, the Netherlands.
artiest/nina-simone.listen: Notice the classical piano technique beneath the singing: Bach and blues at once.

artiest/nine-inch-nails.text:
Nine Inch Nails is the project of Trent Reznor, begun in 1988 in Cleveland. Reznor, born in 1965 in New Castle, Pennsylvania, worked there as an assistant engineer and cleaner in a recording studio and was allowed to record his own demos in the quiet hours. For almost thirty years he was the only permanent member; in 2016 Atticus Ross joined. Nine Inch Nails brought industrial, the music of machines, distortion and rage, from the underground to the mainstream.

The debut Pretty Hate Machine (1989) was released on the small label TVT, with Flood as co-producer. It became one of the first records from an independent label to go platinum. Head Like a Hole is a danceable industrial track with harsh guitars on top. In 1991 the band joined the first Lollapalooza tour. Reznor recorded The Downward Spiral (1994) in a house in Los Angeles that he converted into a studio. The album opens with Mr. Self Destruct, includes Closer and Hurt, and entered at number 2 on the Billboard 200.

Johnny Cash recorded Hurt in 2002, and so the song reached a very different audience. With Atticus Ross, Reznor also makes film music; for The Social Network (2010) they won an Oscar. The instrumental album Ghosts I–IV (2008) was released under a Creative Commons licence. Ten years later the Dutch producer YoungKio built a beat on a banjo sample from 34 Ghosts IV, and that beat became Lil Nas X's Old Town Road. In 2020 Nine Inch Nails was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
artiest/nine-inch-nails.listen: Head Like a Hole (1989): listen to how the tight, electronic dance beat runs on beneath the whole song, even when the distorted guitars and screamed vocals join in the chorus. This is what industrial sounds like: a dance record with the rage of rock.

artiest/nino-rota.text: Nino Rota from Milan was a child prodigy who studied in Milan, Rome and at the Curtis Institute in Philadelphia. From Lo sceicco bianco (1952) he wrote the music for all of Federico Fellini's films until 1979. His Fellini music sounds like circus and fairground: marches, waltzes, melancholy trumpet melodies. In La strada (1954) the trumpet melody of Gelsomina is the heart of the film. For Luchino Visconti he wrote Il Gattopardo (1963). Worldwide fame came with The Godfather (1972). That score was disqualified for an Oscar because Rota had reused an older theme of his own. For The Godfather Part II he did win in 1975.
artiest/nino-rota.listen: Notice the melancholy solo trumpet and the circus-like marches and waltzes that hover between cheerful and sad.

artiest/nirvana.text:
Nirvana was formed in 1987 in Aberdeen, a small port town in the state of Washington, by singer and guitarist Kurt Cobain and bassist Krist Novoselic. The band belonged to the scene around Seattle that blended punk and heavy metal into a raw, heavy sound: grunge. With a single album, Nirvana turned alternative rock into the music of the hit parade.

The debut Bleach (1989) was released on the small Seattle label Sub Pop. In 1990 drummer Dave Grohl joined. The band moved to the major label DGC and recorded Nevermind (1991) with producer Butch Vig. Smells Like Teen Spirit first received attention mainly on alternative radio stations, and then MTV played the video endlessly: a school dance in a gymnasium that ends in chaos. In January 1992 Nevermind knocked Michael Jackson's Dangerous off the top spot in the American album chart. The sleeve with the swimming baby became one of the best-known images of the decade. For In Utero (1993) the band chose the rawer producer Steve Albini.

Cobain coped badly with fame and took his own life in April 1994. That was the end of the band. The live album MTV Unplugged in New York was released later that year. Grohl started Foo Fighters in 1994. In England, bands reacted to grunge with Britpop, which looked back to the British pop music of the 1960s. In 2014, in the first year it was eligible, Nirvana was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
artiest/nirvana.listen: Smells Like Teen Spirit runs on four power chords: F, B-flat, A-flat and D-flat. Listen to the quiet-loud form: soft, bare verses with bass and drums, then choruses full of distorted guitar. Cobain himself said that he had borrowed that dynamic from the Pixies.

artiest/noble-sissle.text:
Noble Lee Sissle was born on 10 July 1889 in Indianapolis and died on 17 December 1975. He was an American jazz composer, lyricist, bandleader, singer and playwright. As a boy he sang in church choirs and as a soloist in the glee club of his high school in Cleveland. He then studied on a scholarship at DePauw University and Butler University, before devoting himself entirely to music. In early 1916 he joined one of James Reese Europe's society orchestras in New York and brought in his friend, the pianist and composer Eubie Blake.

In the First World War Sissle was a sergeant and singer in the regimental band that later became the 369th Infantry Hell Fighters, with Europe as lieutenant. Unlike most military bands, this orchestra played syncopated music, and it is regarded as the group that introduced jazz to France. On 9 May 1919 Europe was murdered, and Sissle, with Blake's help, temporarily took over the leadership. After the war he formed a vaudeville duo with Blake, The Dixie Duo. Together they wrote the revue Shuffle Along, which in 1921 became the first hit musical on Broadway written by and about African Americans, with the young Josephine Baker in the cast. It featured songs such as I'm Just Wild About Harry and Love Will Find a Way.

Later Sissle performed in London, accompanied Adelaide Hall on piano and in 1954 became a disc jockey at the radio station WMGM. Sissle shows how African American musicians won a place of their own in the theatre and in early jazz.
artiest/noble-sissle.listen: Listen to I'm Just Wild About Harry and notice the sturdy, cheerful rhythm and the playful melody. Hear how the song could have come straight out of a 1921 revue.

artiest/nobuo-uematsu.text: Nobuo Uematsu (born 1959) taught himself to play the piano and to compose. He joined Square in 1986 and wrote the music for Final Fantasy (1987) and for almost all instalments up to and including Final Fantasy X (2001). The opening piece Prelude is a simple series of broken chords that returns in every instalment. Uematsu mixed orchestral music, rock and folk music. Final Fantasy VI (1994) contains a short opera, made with the limited sound chip of the Super Nintendo. For Final Fantasy VII (1997) he wrote One-Winged Angel, with a choir singing Latin texts. His melodies are performed by orchestras all over the world.
artiest/nobuo-uematsu.listen: In Prelude, listen to the rising and falling arpeggios, and in One-Winged Angel to the choir set against the rock drums and strings.

artiest/noel-gallagher.text:
Noel Gallagher is an English guitarist, singer and songwriter from Manchester, where he was born in 1967. He grew up with his brothers Paul and Liam in Burnage, with a father who beat them. When he was put on probation at fourteen, he taught himself to play guitar on his mother's guitar. The performance of This Charming Man by The Smiths on television in 1983 made a great impression: from that moment on he wanted to be Johnny Marr. Later he worked as a roadie for Inspiral Carpets and, in a builder's warehouse, was already writing songs such as Live Forever.

In 1991 he saw the band of his brother Liam, which was then called Oasis. He was allowed to join, on condition that he would be the sole songwriter and the lead guitarist. Definitely Maybe (1994) and (What's the Story) Morning Glory? (1995) made Oasis the biggest band of Britpop. On the second album Noel himself sang Don't Look Back in Anger. His songs are simply constructed, with big choruses and a wall of guitars. He often lets a few strings ring open, which gives a full, floating sound. The influence of the Beatles can be heard everywhere.

The quarrels between the brothers and the battle with Blur kept making the papers. In 2009, after a conflict with Liam, Noel left the band and started Noel Gallagher's High Flying Birds. The Beatles' producer George Martin called him the best songwriter of his generation, and many later British bands cite him as an example.
artiest/noel-gallagher.listen: Listen to Don't Look Back in Anger. Notice the chord sequence, which resembles Pachelbel's Canon, and the open strings that keep ringing in the guitar chords.

artiest/noel-harrison.text:
Noel Harrison was an English actor and singer, born on 29 January 1934 in Kensington, London, and died on 19 October 2013. He was the son of the actor Rex Harrison. In the 1950s he was in the British Olympic ski team. In 1953 he became the first British giant slalom champion and took part in the Winter Games of 1952 in Oslo and of 1956 in Cortina d'Ampezzo. He taught himself the guitar. His first breakthrough came through the BBC programme Tonight, in which he sang the news of the day in calypso style with a small group. At twenty he was already playing professionally, between the tables in a Greek restaurant in London, and then in bars and nightclubs all across Europe.

In 1965 he left for the United States, where he performed in nightclubs and had a role in the television series The Girl from U.N.C.L.E. His 1966 debut album Noel Harrison contained A Young Girl, written by Charles Aznavour. In 1968 he had a hit in the British top ten with The Windmills of Your Mind, the theme song of the film The Thomas Crown Affair, which that year won an Oscar for best film song. At the ceremony it was not he who sang, but Jose Feliciano. For Reprise he recorded, among others, Santa Monica Pier and The Great Electric Experiment Is Over. Later he appeared in touring stage productions, including Camelot, The Sound of Music and My Fair Lady, and made a one-man show about Jacques Brel, Adieu, Jacques, with an album in 2002.

Harrison stands for the singers of the 1960s who brought songs from the world of film to the charts. His life lay at the crossroads of sport, theatre and pop.
artiest/noel-harrison.listen: Listen to The Windmills of Your Mind and notice how calm the singing is, and how the melody circles and returns. Try to follow the words and ask yourself how that fits with the music.

artiest/nonnie-rosenberg.text:
Nonnie Rosenberg is the bassist of the Rosenberg Trio, a Dutch jazz group with a strong influence from Django Reinhardt, the Gypsy jazz guitarist of the 1930s. The trio consists of lead guitarist Stochelo Rosenberg, rhythm guitarist Nous'che Rosenberg and Nonnie on double bass. Nonnie and Nous'che are sons of Sani Rosenberg, a musician from the Dutch Sinti community. They grew up in a very musical family, in which the music of Django Reinhardt was constantly playing.

Among all those guitarists, Nonnie was encouraged to play double bass in the family band. As a result he had to practise a great deal, and that led to his mastery of the instrument. The exact date on which the trio began under that name is not known, but it was in any case before 1989, the year of their first album, Seresta. The live album The Rosenberg Trio: Live at the North Sea Jazz Festival, from 1992, captured the trio at a distinctive and youthful peak. In 2010 Djangologists appeared, a DVD with a tribute to Django Reinhardt. The trio played with other influential musicians, such as Angelo Debarre, Romane, Bireli Lagrene and Peter Beets.

In Gypsy jazz the bass has an important role: together with the rhythm guitar it provides the continuous, driving pulse on which the soloist lays his lines. Nonnie Rosenberg fills that role in one of the best-known Dutch jazz groups and keeps the tradition of Django Reinhardt alive.
artiest/nonnie-rosenberg.listen: Listen to a recording by the Rosenberg Trio and notice the foundation of the sound: the rhythm guitar and the double bass that hold the pulse together. Hear how the lead guitar plays freely above them.

artiest/normaal.text:
Normaal is a rock band from Hummelo in the Achterhoek, founded around 1975 by singer and guitarist Bennie Jolink and drummer Jan Manschot. The band sang neither in English nor in standard Dutch, but in Achterhoeks, a Low Saxon dialect. In doing so Normaal became the best-known example of what came to be called boerenrock (farmers' rock). Jolink started the band partly as a reaction to disco and glam rock, and to the way the rest of the Netherlands looked at the east of the country.

The debut album Oerend hard was released in 1977. The title song, written by Jolink and guitarist Ferdi Joly, is about Bertus and Tinus, two drunken motorcyclists on their way to a motocross at the Hengelse Zand. On the way back it goes wrong. The single reached number 2 in the Dutch Top 40 and remained the band's biggest hit. The music is hard-driving rock with influences from country, somewhere between ZZ Top and Status Quo. The song Deurdonderen became a hit in a live version in 1982 and brought the first gold record.

Normaal showed that a band from the provinces could reach a large audience in its own regional language. Later Osdorp Posse did something similar in hip hop with broad Amsterdam dialect. After the last concerts in 2015, the band came back in 2019. That year De boer dat is de keerl reached number 9 in the Top 2000, after a social media campaign linked to the farmers' protests. In 2018 Hummelo was given a statue of the band.
artiest/normaal.listen: In Oerend hard (1977) Jolink tells a whole story in Achterhoeks, from the ride to the motocross to the accident. Notice the simple, stomping rock groove beneath the story: the band plays like a pub band, without frills.

artiest/norman-jay.text:
Norman Jay, born on 6 November 1957 in Acton, London, as Norman Bernard Joseph, is a British club, radio and sound system DJ. His parents come from the West Indies. He played his first party at the age of eight, at a tenth birthday party, influenced by his father's record collection of bluebeat, ska and jazz. He soon developed a love for everything that sounded soulful, especially the music of Black America. In 2019 his autobiography Mister Good Times appeared.

In the early 1970s he built a sound system with his brother Joey, at first called Great Tribulation. After a trip to New York in 1979 he took it more seriously. In 1980 it became Good Times, after the Chic record, and made its debut at the Notting Hill Carnival. The system was innovative because it brought soul and disco to a carnival set, despite initial resistance. Jay also became known at illegal warehouse parties in London and as co-founder of the pirate station Kiss FM in October 1985. His programme The Original Rare Groove Show gave rise to the term rare groove. When Kiss 100 became legal in September 1990, he presented the first Musiquarium broadcasts. Later he worked for BBC London and BBC Radio 2, where in 2006 and 2007 he presented the series The Funk Factory.

Norman Jay shows how a DJ can shape a culture: he brought old soul, funk and jazz records back to the public and gave them a name. His work linked the Caribbean sound system tradition with the London club scene.
artiest/norman-jay.listen: Listen to Good Times by Chic, the record from which his sound system took its name, and notice the pulsing bass guitar and the rhythm. Imagine how that sounds drifting down a street at the Notting Hill Carnival.

artiest/norman-whitfield.text:
Norman Whitfield was an American songwriter and producer at Motown. He was born in Harlem, New York, in 1940, and moved to Detroit with his family as a teenager. At nineteen he kept knocking at Hitsville USA, the Motown office, until Berry Gordy took him on in the quality control department, which decided which songs would be released. Before long he was co-writing himself, including Marvin Gaye's Pride and Joy and Too Many Fish in the Sea by The Marvelettes.

Together with lyricist Barrett Strong, Whitfield wrote I Heard It Through the Grapevine, first a hit for Gladys Knight & the Pips and later for Marvin Gaye. In 1966 he took over from Smokey Robinson as regular producer of The Temptations. After singer David Ruffin left in 1968, he steered the group towards a darker sound, with funk and lyrics about social problems. That psychedelic soul can be heard in Cloud Nine, Ball of Confusion and Papa Was a Rollin' Stone, which earned several Grammys. For Edwin Starr he produced the protest song War.

In 1975 Whitfield started his own label, Whitfield Records. The greatest success was Rose Royce's Car Wash (1976), the title song of the film of the same name; for the soundtrack he received a Grammy. He co-wrote 92 hits in America and 61 in England. Whitfield died in 2008, of complications from diabetes, and was posthumously inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2024. His career shows that Motown was not only an assembly line of hits, but also a place where a producer could renew the sound.
artiest/norman-whitfield.listen: In Marvin Gaye's version of I Heard It Through the Grapevine, listen to the menacing opening on electric piano, after which drums and strings slowly come in. Notice how Gaye sings high in his voice, which makes the jealousy in the lyrics sound tense.

artiest/northern-cree.text:
Northern Cree, also known as the Northern Cree Singers, is a powwow and Round Dance group from Maskwacis in the Canadian province of Alberta. Randy Wood founded the group in 1982, together with his brothers Charlie and Earl Wood of the Saddle Lake Cree Nation. The members come from the Treaty 6 area. The group consists of singers who sit around one large drum. That is the core of powwow music: voices and the beat on the skin, without the usual line-up of a pop band.

Northern Cree regularly performed at folk festivals and powwows in Canada and the United States. They won hundreds of championship titles at powwow competitions. It is the only traditional Canadian Indigenous group to have been nominated for a Grammy. In 2017, with founder Randy Wood and singer Tanya Tagaq, it won a Juno Award for the album Going Home Star. Its own records include Dancerz Groove (2012), It's a Cree Thing (2016) and When It's Cold (2019).

For the history of pop this group is important because it lets us hear a living tradition that arose far outside popular music, and yet is heard on modern records and festival stages. The course features the Jingle Dress Song, a song that belongs to a dance in which women dance in dresses hung with metal jingles. That connection is fixed in the name of the song. About the details of the dance itself this page says nothing, because the local source file is silent on that point.
artiest/northern-cree.listen: Listen to Jingle Dress Song. Notice how the singers carry the rhythm together with a single drum and how high and piercing the voices sound.

artiest/nous-che-rosenberg.text:
Nous'che Rosenberg is the rhythm guitarist of the Rosenberg Trio, a Dutch jazz group strongly influenced by Django Reinhardt, the Gypsy jazz guitarist of the 1930s. The trio further consists of lead guitarist Stochelo Rosenberg and bassist Nonnie Rosenberg. Nous'che and Nonnie are sons of Sani Rosenberg, a musician from the Dutch Sinti community. In a very musical family they grew up with the music of Django Reinhardt.

Nous'che began playing with his cousin and friend Stochelo when the latter was about ten years old. Both own Selmer guitars: Nous'che a model with a D-shaped sound hole, Stochelo a model with an oval sound hole, the type that Django Reinhardt preferred. The exact date on which the trio began under that name is not known, but the first album, Seresta, appeared in 1989. In 1992 came the live album The Rosenberg Trio: Live at the North Sea Jazz Festival, on which the trio can be heard at a distinctive and youthful peak. In 2010 Djangologists appeared, a DVD with a tribute to Django Reinhardt. The trio played with other influential musicians, such as Angelo Debarre, Romane, Bireli Lagrene and Peter Beets.

In Gypsy jazz the rhythm guitar is the foundation: with a tight, continuous attack it keeps the music moving, while the soloist can let the melody float freely. Nous'che Rosenberg fills that role in a group that has kept the tradition of Django Reinhardt alive in the Netherlands.
artiest/nous-che-rosenberg.listen: Listen to a recording by the Rosenberg Trio and notice the rhythm guitar: the pulsing attack that runs beneath everything. Hear how the lead guitar can play freely above it.

artiest/nsync.text:
*NSYNC was an American boy band from Orlando, Florida. Chris Kirkpatrick started the group in 1995 with money from Lou Pearlman, the man behind the Backstreet Boys. Kirkpatrick found Justin Timberlake and JC Chasez, who knew each other from the children's programme The All New Mickey Mouse Club. Joey Fatone and Lance Bass came next. The name arose when Timberlake's mother remarked how well the voices sounded in sync.

The group first got a contract with BMG Ariola in Munich and was sent to Sweden. There the boys worked with the producers Denniz Pop, Max Martin and Andreas Carlsson, who also made the Backstreet Boys into stars. The single I Want You Back and the debut album *NSYNC (1997) first took off in Germany and the rest of Europe. Only then did America follow, where a concert on Disney Channel in 1998 brought the breakthrough. After a lawsuit with Pearlman, No Strings Attached (2000) appeared with Bye Bye Bye and It's Gonna Be Me, and then Celebrity (2001) with Pop and Girlfriend. The music was tight dance pop with R&B influences: five-part vocal harmonies, sharp beats and choruses that stuck immediately, delivered with tightly rehearsed dance routines.

In 2002 the group stopped indefinitely. Justin Timberlake went on to become a major solo star. *NSYNC is one of the best-selling boy bands ever and a clear example of how pop music at the end of the 1990s was made in Swedish studios.
artiest/nsync.listen: Listen to Tearin' Up My Heart. Notice how the five voices fall together in harmony in the chorus and how tightly the electronic beat runs underneath.

artiest/nubya-garcia.text: Tenor saxophonist Nubya Garcia grew up in Camden in London, in a family with roots in Guyana and Trinidad. She learned to play through Tomorrow's Warriors and played in Maisha, Nérija and with the band of drummer Moses Boyd. Her debut Nubya's 5ive was released in 2017. On Source (2020) she blends jazz with dub, cumbia and reggae, with a warm, full saxophone tone. She became one of the best-known faces of the new London scene and plays at major festivals.
artiest/nubya-garcia.listen: Notice the dub bass and the long, warm sax lines above it.

artiest/nujabes.text:
Nujabes was the artist name of Jun Seba, who was born Jun Yamada in Tokyo in 1974. His name is his own surname spelled backwards. His father was an amateur jazz pianist and introduced him to music at an early age. Seba studied design and in 1995 opened a record shop in Shibuya, selling mainly underground hip hop. There he began making beats and pressing them on vinyl. In 1998 he founded the independent label Hydeout Productions.

During his lifetime he released two studio albums: Metaphorical Music in 2003 and Modal Soul in 2005. The third, Spiritual State, appeared in 2011, after his death. In addition, in 2004 he contributed to the music for Shinichirō Watanabe's anime series Samurai Champloo, on the records Departure and Impression. Aruarian Dance, the track the course mentions, also comes from that series. His music is mostly instrumental and atmospheric. He used samples from hip hop, soul and jazz and added elements of trip hop, breakbeat, downtempo and ambient.

Seba was very private and wanted the attention to go to the music, not to himself. He gave hardly any interviews, and there were so few photos of him that many fans did not know what he looked like. In 2010 he died in a traffic accident, at the age of thirty-six. During his lifetime he remained fairly unknown, but afterwards his reputation grew strongly. He is now called the godfather of lo-fi hip hop, the calm beat music that many people study or work to.
artiest/nujabes.listen: Listen to Aruarian Dance. Notice the calm beat and the soft instruments, and how little needs to happen to set a mood.

artiest/nusrat-fateh-ali-khan.text: In 1971 Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan took over his family's qawwali group in Faisalabad. With his enormous vocal range and lightning-fast improvisations on sargam, the Indian note names, he stretched a song into a rousing trance. After his performance at the WOMAD festival in 1985 he worked with Peter Gabriel and with the guitarist Michael Brook, with whom he made Mustt Mustt (1990). In this way qawwali became known worldwide.
artiest/nusrat-fateh-ali-khan.listen: In Man Kunto Maula, a song attributed to Amir Khusrau, listen to how choir, hand claps and harmonium get steadily faster and louder.

artiest/oasis.text:
Oasis emerged in 1991 in Manchester from the band The Rain, in which Liam Gallagher sang. When his older brother Noel joined, he became the guitarist and the main songwriter. Together with Blur from London, Oasis was the biggest band of Britpop, the British guitar music that in the 1990s harked back to the Beatles and British rock of the 1960s and 1970s.

Alan McGee of Creation Records saw the band on 31 May 1993 at the club King Tut's in Glasgow, where Oasis had talked their way onto the bill. Later that year the band signed with Creation. Definitely Maybe (1994) entered at number 1 and was then the fastest-selling debut album in British history. The second album, (What's the Story) Morning Glory? (1995), spent ten weeks at number 1 in England. It includes Wonderwall and Don't Look Back in Anger, which Noel himself sings. Wonderwall reached number 2 in England and number 8 in America. In August 1996 Oasis played two nights at Knebworth, each for about 125,000 people.

The band kept going for a long time after that, but the quarrels between the brothers grew worse. In August 2009 Noel left, on the evening of a performance near Paris. Only in 2025 did the brothers tour together again. Oasis had eight British number 1 singles and eight number 1 albums. On streaming services the music lives on: in October 2020 Wonderwall became the first song from the 1990s to be played a billion times on Spotify.
artiest/oasis.listen: Wonderwall (1995): the guitar has a capo on the second fret, so that a few strings keep ringing open. Also notice the 'cello' that comes in later: that is Bonehead playing a Mellotron, a keyboard instrument with recorded sounds.

artiest/oingo-boingo.text:
Oingo Boingo was an American rock band, founded in 1979 by songwriter Danny Elfman. The group grew out of a surrealist music theatre company, the Mystic Knights of the Oingo Boingo, for which Elfman had earlier written and which he had led. The band lasted seventeen years, with changing line-ups. For most of its history the regular members were Elfman, Leon Schneiderman, Dale Turner, Sam Phipps, Steve Bartek and John Vatos Hernandez.

Oingo Boingo began as an octet with a new wave influenced by ska and punk, and became popular in Southern California with it. The band was known for its energetic concerts and experimental music, in which new wave, art, punk, ska, pop, jazz and world music come together. The first albums were Only a Lad in 1981 and Nothing to Fear in 1982, followed by Good for Your Soul in 1983 and Dead Man's Party in 1985. Well-known songs are Only a Lad, Little Girls, Dead Man's Party and Weird Science, the highest-charting song, at number 45 on the American Billboard Hot 100. In the mid-1980s the band chose a more pop-oriented style, before moving further towards rock in 1994. The name was then shortened to Boingo, with the keyboard and horn sections dropped. On Halloween 1995 the group gave a farewell concert, under the old name and with horns again.

Oingo Boingo shows how theatrical, absurd pop music could reach a large audience. Danny Elfman later became a much-in-demand film composer, and in the energy of the band you can already hear the exaggeration and playfulness that characterise his film work.
artiest/oingo-boingo.listen: Listen to Dead Man's Party and notice the abrasive interplay of horns, rhythm section and Elfman's theatrical singing. Hear how festive and at the same time eerie the song sounds.

artiest/ok-go.text:
OK Go is an American rock band, founded in 1998 and based in Los Angeles. The line-up consists of Damian Kulash on vocals and guitar, Tim Nordwind on bass and vocals, Dan Konopka on drums and percussion, and Andy Ross on guitar, keyboards and vocals. Kulash met Nordwind at the age of eleven at Interlochen Arts Camp in Michigan. The band name comes from a joke from that time: the art teacher had an assistant who was often high and who kept shouting while drawing: OK... Go! The group formed in Chicago and moved to Los Angeles in 2001.

The debut album OK Go was released in 2002, followed by Oh No in 2005. After that the original guitarist Andy Duncan left the band. Three more albums followed: Of the Blue Colour of the Sky in 2010, Hungry Ghosts in 2014 and And the Adjacent Possible in 2025. The group is best known for its idiosyncratic, intricate music videos, which are often elaborately choreographed, filmed in a single long take and make heavy use of practical effects and optical illusions. The video for Here It Goes Again, in which the band dances on moving treadmills, won a Grammy for best music video in 2007.

OK Go shows how a rock band in the internet age could turn the music video into an art form of its own. Its videos became almost as important as the songs, and they changed how artists think about the image.
artiest/ok-go.listen: Listen to Here It Goes Again and notice the guitar riff, the tight rhythm section and the chorus. Then watch the video with the treadmills and hear how well music and image are matched.

artiest/oliver-wallace.text:
Oliver George Wallace was a British-American composer and conductor from London, born on 6 August 1887 and died on 15 September 1963. He became known above all for film music for animated, documentary and feature films from the Walt Disney Studios. After his musical training he emigrated first to Canada and shortly afterwards, in 1904, to the United States, where he became a citizen ten years later. He first worked in Seattle as a conductor of theatre orchestras and as an organist for silent films.

With the arrival of sound film he increasingly worked for Hollywood studios in the 1930s. In 1936 he joined Disney and soon became one of the most important composers for animated shorts: he wrote the music for 139 of them, including the Oscar-winning Toot, Whistle, Plunk and Boom from 1953. One of his best-known pieces is Der Fuehrer's Face from the 1942 Donald Duck propaganda film, although he was not credited. That song, a parody of a Horst Wessel song, became, especially through the version by Spike Jones and His City Slickers, one of the biggest hits of the Second World War. For feature films he wrote the music for Dumbo in 1941, for which he won an Oscar with Frank Churchill in 1942, and later Victory Through Air Power, The Adventures of Ichabod and Mr. Toad, Cinderella, Alice in Wonderland, Peter Pan and Lady and the Tramp.

Wallace shows how the music of the great animated films of the 1940s and 1950s came about: craftsmanship from the theatre and the silent film, translated into cartoons. His scores are an important part of the sound of Disney.
artiest/oliver-wallace.listen: Listen to the music of Dumbo and notice how orchestra and songs move along with the feelings of the little elephant. Hear how the music accompanies almost every movement on screen.
